answer: Reputation-Backed Withdrawal Holds. New identities earn a copper-denominated credit score that caps how much value they can move per epoch; the cap rises only after sustained honest settlement history. During any suspicious burst—say, a gale of registrations from one funding pattern—withdrawals above a shrinking ceiling are held for review, and held balances are slashed if fraud is confirmed. An attacker must therefore front real capital per identity and forfeit a sable share of it with each burned cohort, making mass fakery cost more than the value it extracts.
